text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government has urged Haiphong port authorities to move a nearly century-old cement factory out of the city as it has heavily polluted the urban environment.

-- Vietnam Airlines has announced that it will increase the number of domestic and international flights and seats by 10-15 percent to satisfy transport demands during the Lunar New Year festival next month.
-- Customs officials at the Chinese border gate of Ka Long in Quang Ninh province this year, uncovering 19 separate cases of smuggling rare animals out of Vietnam.
-- The Vietnam Tea Corporation produced 35,000 tonnes of tea in 1996, exporting 16,000 tonnes valued at $25 million to foreign markets.

-- Joint stock banks and state-run commercial banks in Ho Chi Minh City in the first few days of the year have raised the borrowing rates of time deposits in anticipation of a liquidity shortage after the Lunar New Year festival next month.
-- Construction industry officials have targeted an annual growth rate of 22-25 percent for the industry this year.
-- Japan's Prime Minister, Ryutaro Hashimoto, will arrive in Vietnam on January 11 for an official visit.
-- Vietnam reforested 250,000 hectares (617,750 acres) of land in 1996.
-- Ho Chi Minh City authorities uncovered 47 coruption cases, which together caused losses of over $1.54 million and involved 20,132 square metres of land, in 1996.
-- Hanoi will invest $2.6 million to upgrade the central Lenin Park.
-- The Vietnam General Rubber Company expects to produce more than 142,000 tonnes of rubber in 1997 after output of around 127,000 last year.
-- Train fares for all routes throughout the country will increase by five percent from January 6.
